exposure: Non-medically indicated induction of labor at 39 weeks' gestation
cohort: 455,044 nulliparous women with low-risk pregnancies in California between 2007 and 2011
finding: Non-medically indicated induction of labor at 39 weeks' gestation was associated with a lower rate of cesarean births and some maternal and neonatal adverse outcomes in most hospital settings, except for low-volume hospitals where the difference in cesarean birth rates was not significant.
mod_finding: Non-medically indicated induction of labor at 39 weeks gestation may be associated with a lower rate of cesarean births compared to expectant management in various hospital settings.
